newsitem.title: USA: Transamerica settles suit, to take Q1 charge.
newsitem.headline: Transamerica settles suit, to take Q1 charge.

text.p: Transamerica Corp on Friday said its life-insurance subsidiaries entered a proposed settlement of a class-action lawsuit regarding the sale and performance of some of its universal and whole life insurance policies.
The company said its first-quarter results would reflect about $20 million of costs related to the suit, including the plaintiff's attorney fees and expenses.
The lawsuit involved Transamerica Occidental Life Insurance Co, Transamerica Assurance Co and First Transamerica Life Insurance Co

Transamerica said the settlement would provide $125 million to $135 million in benefits to policyholders, excluding benefits awarded through the claim review process, which a policyholder could invoke if unsatisfied with the settlement.
A company spokesman said the $125 million to $135 million was not a cash payout but instead represented the economic value of benefits to policyholders.
He did not estimate what the benefits would mean to the company in terms of unrecognized profit.
The spokesman also said that the company did not believe the claims review process would add much liability.
He said the company was convinced that there was no pattern of wrongdoing and that it settled the suit because it felt it was in its best interests.
A hearing regarding approval of the settlement is scheduled for June 26.
